s01.text: Most people switch on Airplane Mode believing it makes their battery soak up electricity faster.

s02.text: In reality, the charging circuit doesn't pull a single extra watt. Airplane Mode charges faster because your radio transmitters stop wasting the power.

s03.text: When cellular signal is weak, your phone's radio power amplifiers ramp up from twenty milliwatts to over two thousand milliwatts just searching for towers.

s04.text: Plugged into a basic five-watt charger, active cellular pings, Wi-Fi beacons, and Bluetooth scanning burn up to forty percent of incoming electricity.

s05.text: Even worse, that dissipated radio power produces heat inside the chassis, forcing the battery management chip to throttle incoming current to protect the cell.

s06.text: Airplane Mode shuts off baseband transmission entirely, channeling one hundred percent of incoming wattage straight into battery chemistry.

s07.text: On a sixty-five-watt brick the difference is tiny, but on a low-power charger, Airplane Mode isn't a turbo switch: it's plugging a massive leak.
